result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_isomorphic()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if this graph is isomorphic to another graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L4545-L4647){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_isomorphic(other) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Two graphs are isomorphic if there exists a one-to-one correspondence (bijection) between their nodes that preserves the adjacency relationship. In simpler terms, they have the same structure but possibly different node labels. This implementation checks the following necessary conditions: - same number of nodes - same number of edges - same degree sequence - same directedness ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [other]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Another `Graph` object to compare with. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if graphs satisfy isomorphism conditions, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} This is a heuristic check using necessary but not sufficient conditions. It will correctly identify *non-isomorphic* graphs (returning `False`) but may give false positives. A complete isomorphism test requires algorithms like VF2. This method is useful as a fast filter before more expensive isomorphism tests. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Same graph structure with different labels: ::: {#a55d992d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g1 = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) g2 = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="X") .add_node(label="Y") .add_node(label="Z") .add_edge("X", "Y") .add_edge("Y", "Z") ) # Returns True (both are paths of length 2) g1.is_isomorphic(g2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Different structures are not isomorphic: ::: {#a2c9c05e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} path = ec.Graph(directed=False).add_path_graph(n=4) star = ec.Graph(directed=False).add_star_graph(n=4) # Returns False (different degree sequences) path.is_isomorphic(star) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Directed vs undirected are not isomorphic: ::: {#4e193b33 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} directed = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_path_graph(n=3) undirected = ec.Graph(directed=False).add_path_graph(n=3) # Returns False (different directedness) directed.is_isomorphic(undirected) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Complete graphs of same size: ::: {#2996f3be .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} k4_a = ec.Graph(directed=False).add_full_graph(n=4) k4_b = ec.Graph(directed=False).add_full_graph(n=4) # Returns True (same structure) k4_a.is_isomorphic(k4_b) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Different sized graphs: ::: {#a1101df9 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} g3 = ec.Graph(directed=False).add_cycle_graph(n=3) g4 = ec.Graph(directed=False).add_cycle_graph(n=4) # Returns False (different sizes) g3.is_isomorphic(g4) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` False ``` ::: :::
